name: ChooseWow - Email 2: The Habit That Survives
subject: The habit that survived my busiest year
body:
✦ ChooseWow

Hey {{ .Subscriber.FirstName }},

Quick question: What habit do you wish you could stick to?

I ask because I want to tell you about 2019 — the year that almost broke me.

"Mailigen was being acquired by Pipedrive. I was transitioning from founder to VP of Product. Moving countries. Learning new systems. Meeting new teams. Everything was changing, constantly."

Most of my routines disappeared. Morning runs? Gone (new city, no route). Meditation? Forgotten (different schedule). Reading before bed? Impossible (too exhausted).

But one habit survived everything.

Every night, before sleep, I wrote three lines:

• One thing I learned today
• One person who helped me
• One moment I want to remember

Not because I'm disciplined. Because it was too simple to fail.

Three lines. 90 seconds. Even on 14-hour days in conference rooms, arguing about product roadmaps.

Here's what I noticed after 6 months:

The chaos felt more manageable. Not because it got easier, but because I started seeing progress inside the mess. Learning. Help. Good moments. They were always there — I just wasn't noticing them.

"The simplest practices survive the hardest times. And those are usually when you need them most."

This is why the 5-Minute Reset from last week works. It's not about finding 30 minutes for meditation or journaling pages. It's about building something so simple that it survives your worst days.

Your turn: What's one tiny practice you could do even on your busiest day? Hit reply and tell me. I read everything, and I often share insights (with permission) in future emails.

Remember: Progress over perfection, always.

— Janis
